locator: can. 749 §§2-3, qui, ut fidei et morum doctores et iudices, pro universa Ecclesia doctrinam de fide vel de moribus definitive tenendam declarant
interpretation: Can. 749 §2: 'Infallibilitate in magisterio pollet quoque Collegium Episcoporum quando magisterium exercent Episcopi in Concilio Oecumenico coadunati, qui, ut fidei et morum doctores et iudices, pro universa Ecclesia doctrinam de fide vel de moribus definitive tenendam declarant'; §3: 'Infallibiliter definita nulla intellegitur doctrina, nisi id manifesto constiterit.' (The page spells 'Infallibiitate'.) The canon is about definitive declarations; whether a given canon of Dei Filius is such a declaration is not stated here.
attribution: The passage states that bishops gathered in an ecumenical council, as teachers and judges of faith and morals for the universal Church, teach infallibly when they declare a doctrine to be held definitively, and that nothing counts as infallibly defined unless this is manifest, which is the premise.
